title: Violence in Amsterdam around the Ajax and Maccabi Tel Aviv match
body:
Maccabi Tel Aviv supporters arrived in Amsterdam on 6 November 2024 for a Europa League match against Ajax. Police said Maccabi fans burned a Palestinian flag in Dam Square and vandalised a taxi, and a city council member said Israeli fans attacked houses displaying Palestinian flags. On 7 November Maccabi supporters chanted anti-Arab slogans on their march to the stadium, and Ajax won the match 5-0 without incident inside the ground.

After the match, groups on scooters targeted Maccabi fans heading to the city centre, and riot police intervened. Order was restored by about 3 a.m. on 8 November. Police detained 62 people and deployed 600 additional officers. Five people were hospitalised and released. Police said 20 to 30 people had minor injuries, while Israel's foreign ministry said 10 Israelis were hurt.

Mayor Femke Halsema described the attacks as anti-Semitic hit-and-run squads and imposed a three-day demonstration ban from 8 to 10 November, along with stop-and-search powers and a face-covering ban. Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu ordered Mossad to draft a plan to prevent violence at international events. President Joe Biden called the attacks despicable, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres expressed shock, and UEFA said it would investigate.
